sections.h2: What is Caddo Parish and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Caddo Parish is in the northwest corner of Louisiana, with Shreveport as its parish seat and largest city. Wikipedia's parish entry reports a 2020 population of 237,848 and a total area of 937 square miles, about 58 of them water. Shreveport grew along the Red River and is the center of the Ark-La-Tex region.

The legislature created the parish in 1838 from Natchitoches Parish and named it for the Caddo people. Bossier Parish lies directly east, across the river, with Arkansas to the north and Texas to the west and southwest. The parish holds eleven incorporated places, which gives owners several different local governments to deal with.

TypePlaces in Caddo Parish
CityShreveport
TownsBlanchard, Greenwood, Mooringsport, Oil City, Vivian
VillagesBelcher, Gilliam, Hosston, Ida, Rodessa
Other named communitiesLakeview (census-designated place), Keithville, Dixie, Zylks and others

Interstates 20, 220 and 49 cross the parish, along with U.S. 71, 79, 80 and 171.

sections.h2: What does the Caddo Parish economy look like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Most of the parish economy runs through Shreveport, and the numbers show uneven incomes. Wikipedia names Amazon and Walmart among the large employers and lists LSU Health Sciences Center in Shreveport. It also reports that about 22.9% of residents lived at or below the poverty line in 2020, and that parishwide median household income was $42,003 in the 2020 American Community Survey.

Those figures matter to sellers because an owner on a tight income can fall behind on a bill that arrives once a year, and the parish runs an annual tax lien auction for unpaid balances.

The Caddo Parish School Board runs the public schools across the whole parish.

sections.h2: Who handles Caddo Parish property tax?
sections.html:
The Caddo Parish Assessor values every parcel and the Caddo Parish Sheriff collects the parish tax. The Sheriff's FAQ states plainly that the Sheriff does not decide how much you owe, and that the Assessor's Office, in Room 102 of the courthouse, is separate from the Sheriff.

  • Assessor: Caddo Parish Courthouse, Room 102, (318) 226-6701 for address changes and value questions.
  • Sheriff's Tax Department: Caddo Parish Courthouse, 1st Floor, 501 Texas Street, Room 101, Shreveport, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM; phone (318) 681-0638 for balances.
  • Mail payments to the Property Tax Dept., P.O. Box 20905, Shreveport, LA 71120-0905.
  • Shreveport city tax is collected separately by the city, at (318) 673-5500, and does not appear on the Sheriff's notice.

Outside Shreveport, nine parish fire districts provide fire protection, and their fees are set by voters in each district. Shreveport residents fund fire service through city taxes instead.

sections.h2: How does the Caddo assessor set a value?
sections.html:
Caddo uses three approaches: comparing recent sales, estimating replacement cost less depreciation, and looking at the income a property could earn. The Assessor's FAQ also warns that a sale made under pressure, such as an owner who needed cash fast, can distort a comparison, so the office studies many sales.

Louisiana then applies a fixed percentage to the market value to reach the assessed value.

ClassShare of market value assessed
Land10%
Residential improvements, including apartments10%
Commercial improvements15%
Business movable property15%
Public service, excluding land25%

Millage then converts the assessed value to tax. The Sheriff's example at 150 mills puts tax at $1,500 on $10,000 of assessed value, or $375 after a $7,500 homestead exemption. That illustration uses a round rate, so read your own notice for the real one.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for exemptions and freezes in Caddo Parish?
sections.html:
An owner who lives in the home qualifies for the homestead exemption, which removes parish tax on the first $75,000 of market value. It applies to one home, not to city taxes, and not to fire district fees. File as soon as you become the owner; the exemption stays until the owner changes or the home stops being the primary residence.

  • Disabled veterans: a 100% service-connected rating, confirmed by a Veterans Administration form, can qualify for up to $75,000 of additional homestead.
  • Age 65 and older: a special assessment level freezes the assessed value if adjusted gross income was under $100,000. It is lost if the property is transferred or improvements exceed 25% of its value, and a surviving spouse over 55 can qualify.
  • Disabled owners under 65: a freeze is available with 100% Social Security disability or a 50% service-connected rating, but it must be reapplied for each year.

The office requires proof of the previous year's income, such as a tax return or a Social Security statement.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Caddo assessment and appeal dates?
sections.html:
For 2026 the Caddo assessor opened the books on August 17 and closed public inspection on August 31. According to the office's news page, all appeals had to be received by 5:00 p.m. on September 8, and the Board of Review heard appeals on September 14 at 1:00 p.m. at the Caddo Commission.

The Assessor's FAQ explains why timing matters: the open-roll period is when an owner can legally file a protest. Many taxpayers wait for the bill that arrives around the first of December, and the office will discuss the assessment then, but a protest can no longer be filed at that point. If you missed this year's window, mark the late-August dates in next year's calendar.

sections.h2: When is Caddo Parish property tax due and what happens when it is late?
sections.html:
Caddo taxes must be paid by December 31, and the Sheriff's FAQ says notices are generally mailed in the last week of November. After December 31 the tax is delinquent, with interest of 1% per month. Taxes not fully paid by January 31 add a 10% collection fee, and unpaid accounts after that date add the cost of notices and newspaper advertising.

ItemDetail from the Sheriff
Due dateDecember 31
Interest after December 311% per month
Collection fee10% if not fully paid by January 31
Personal or business checksAccepted only until the close of business on the last day of February
Mortgage companiesAsked to pay by December 20; postmarks of December 31 are accepted
2026 tax lien auctionOnline, June 30, 2026

Payments post to the account number you give, and a payment to the wrong account is final. Partial payments are allowed, but the unpaid balance keeps growing and the parcel is still offered at the annual auction.

sections.h2: What happens to a Caddo house at a tax lien auction?
sections.html:
The Sheriff sells a tax lien certificate at an online auction, and the winning bidder is the person who will take the least ownership interest in the property while paying the full unpaid taxes. That description appears in the Caddo Sheriff's FAQ, and it matches the new statewide lien approach that the Bossier Sheriff describes as effective January 1, 2026. A property that draws no bid is transferred to the parish, which can sometimes sell it to a third party.

The Assessor's FAQ adds that adjudicated property can be found through the CPTA Professional Search subscription or by visiting the courthouse, and that phone requests are not answered. Because the rules changed in 2026, a Caddo owner with a delinquent balance should ask the Sheriff what the lien process allows today.

sections.h2: How does Caddo property tax work when you sell?
sections.html:
The Sheriff does not split the bill between buyer and seller, so the full year's tax stays on the property until someone pays it. A buyer who closes after January 1 may find the account still in the prior owner's name, and the Sheriff's FAQ says the new owner is responsible for checking what is owed.

  • Get the current balance from the Sheriff's Tax Department before choosing a closing date.
  • Check city tax with Shreveport separately, since it is billed apart from the parish.
  • Ask your mortgage servicer for proof of payment if escrow covers the tax, because the Sheriff posts the first payment it receives and will not reverse a duplicate.
  • Have the new owner file for homestead soon after closing.

A house with taxes behind can still be sold if the title company pays the balance from proceeds.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Caddo Parish?
faqs.a: The Caddo Parish Sheriff's Tax Department collects parish property tax at 501 Texas Street, Room 101, in Shreveport, or by mail to P.O. Box 20905. The Assessor sets the value but does not take payment.

faqs.q: Is Shreveport city tax on my Caddo Parish tax notice?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff's notice covers parish taxes only. The City of Shreveport collects its own tax and can be reached at (318) 673-5500.

faqs.q: When did Caddo's 2026 assessment appeals close?
faqs.a: Appeals had to reach the assessor by 5:00 p.m. on September 8, 2026, with Board of Review hearings on September 14 at 1:00 p.m. at the Caddo Commission.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for paying Caddo tax late?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 1% per month after December 31. A 10% collection fee applies if the tax is not fully paid by January 31, and notice and advertising costs can follow.

faqs.q: Does the Caddo homestead exemption cover fire district fees?
faqs.a: No. It covers parish tax on the first $75,000 of market value for one home, but not city taxes or fire district fees.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Caddo Parish house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company can pay the delinquent tax, interest and fees from the sale proceeds. Get the payoff amount from the Sheriff's Tax Department first.
